sections.label: NEA high-GWP equipment supply ban
sections.summary: From 1 October next year, NEA will not allow supply of high-GWP RAC equipment, starting with household air-conditioners, refrigerators and commercial water-cooled chillers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: From 1 October next year, NEA will not allow the supply of RAC equipment with high GWP, starting with household air-conditioners that use refrigerants with GWP of more than 750; and household refrigerators and commercial water-cooled chillers that use refrigerants with GWP of more than 15.

sections.label: Low-GWP chiller cost savings
sections.summary: Low-GWP water-cooled chillers cost 15% more on average for commercial users, but energy efficiency means life-cycle savings exceed the higher upfront cost.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: For commercial users, low-GWP water-cooled chillers cost 15% more on average, but as they are more energy-efficient, their life-cycle cost savings more than make up for the higher upfront cost.

sections.label: Supplier and equipment registration
sections.summary: Suppliers must register once, while registration of regulated RAC equipment is valid for three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Suppliers will need to register themselves once, whereas the registration of the regulated RAC equipment will be valid for three years.

sections.label: Temasek Polytechnic chiller course
sections.summary: NEA has worked with Temasek Polytechnic to roll out a course on handling commercial water-cooled chillers this month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: NEA has worked with Temasek Polytechnic to roll out a course on handling commercial water-cooled chillers this month.

sections.label: Requirements start with commercial chillers
sections.summary: The requirements will initially apply only to companies handling commercial water-cooled chillers, which have much larger refrigerant capacities than household air-conditioners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: For a start, these requirements will only apply to companies handling commercial water-cooled chillers, as these chillers have much larger refrigerant capacities than household air-conditioners.

sections.label: Appeals and HFC emission reduction
sections.summary: A person may appeal in writing to the Minister, whose decision is final; the three HFC mitigation measures are expected to halve HFC emissions from regulated equipment by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Thereafter, the person may appeal in writing to the Minister, whose decision will be final.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: These three HFC mitigation measures are expected to reduce HFC emissions from the regulated equipment by around half by the year 2030.

sections.label: NEA grants for quieter construction
sections.summary: From April 2014 to March this year, NEA disbursed $8.3 million in grants to incentivise contractors to adopt quieter construction equipment and methods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Third, from April 2014 to March this year, NEA disbursed a total of $8.3 million in grants to incentivise contractors to adopt quieter construction equipment and methods.

sections.label: Video surveillance for no-work offenders
sections.summary: From 1 October next year, electronic video surveillance will be imposed on a small subset of no-work rule offenders to deter violations and improve NEA's effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: From 1 October next year, we will impose electronic video surveillance on the small subset of offenders to deter further violations of the no-work rule and improve NEA’s operational effectiveness.

sections.label: Notice requirements for surveillance systems
sections.summary: The notice to no-work rule offenders may specify surveillance system type, devices, recorded site area and duration, with storage, NEA access, penalties and appeals to the Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The notice issued to no-work rule offenders may specify the type of surveillance system required; the number of monitoring devices to be installed and where; the part of the construction site to be recorded; and the duration for which the surveillance system must be operational.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The owner or occupier must store the recordings for the period specified in the notice and provide NEA with access to any stored recording so as to facilitate remote monitoring and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The penalties for non-compliance are aligned with those for similar requirements in the Act, such as compliance with noise limits and installation of noise meters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Section 42 is amended to provide for appeals to the Minister against a notice issued by the Director-General under section 28A.

sections.label: Regulating HFC emissions
sections.summary: Reducing HFC emissions, about 7% of Singapore's emissions with high warming potential, supports climate mitigation, and the speaker asks why only household RACs and commercial water-cooled chillers are regulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Reducing HFC emissions, which make up about 7% of Singapore’s emissions, will contribute to our climate mitigation efforts and I wholeheartedly support this move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: HFCs have nearly 12,000 times the warming potential of carbon dioxide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And Singapore is emitting such gases more than ever before, a 30% increase from 2014 to 2016, based on the latest available data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad we are doing more, but my question is: why are household RACs and commercial water-cooled chillers the only equipment being regulated?

sections.label: Review of construction noise limits
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for an update on the review of construction noise limits and whether stricter limits on Saturdays can be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on its review of construction noise limits and also consider whether we can have even stricter construction noise limits on Saturdays?

sections.label: Global CO2 emission reductions
sections.summary: To limit warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius with no or limited overshoot, net global CO2 emissions need to fall about 45% from 2010 levels by 2030 and reach net zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To limit warming to 1.5 degree celsius with no or limited overshoot, net global CO2 emissions need to fall by about 45% from 2010 levels by 2030 and reach "net zero" by 2050.

sections.label: Sea level rise and carbon budgets
sections.summary: Global mean sea level will rise two to three metres over 2,000 years, and remaining carbon budgets are estimated at 500 and 1,350 GtCO2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Over the next 2,000 years, the global mean sea level will rise by about two to three metres, even if warming is limited to 1.5 degree celsius, with the effect irreversible for millennia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At this point in time, remaining carbon budgets for a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5 degree celsius and two degree celcius are estimated at 500 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (GtCO2) and 1,350 GtCO2 respectively.

sections.label: Methane heat trapping power
sections.summary: Methane is less prevalent than CO2 but over 80 times more powerful at trapping heat in the first 10 to 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While methane is less prevalent than CO2, it is more than 80 times more powerful at trapping heat over the first 10 to 20 years in the atmosphere.

sections.label: Refrigerant GWP restrictions
sections.summary: NEA will restrict supply of certain air-conditioning equipment and refrigerators and chillers based on disclosed GWP limits from the fourth quarter of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, according to the NEA website, the typical refrigerant used in chillers is R134a, which has a GWP of 1,300.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The climate-friendly alternative is R1233zd, which has a GWP of just one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on what is disclosed, the NEA will, from the fourth quarter of 2022, restrict the supply of certain air-conditioning equipment with a GWP of more than 750 and certain refrigerators and chillers with GWP of more than 15.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How much of a decline in the percentage or volume of GHG emissions is this restriction expected to lead to?

sections.label: Current penalty for offence
sections.summary: A conviction for this offence currently attracts a fine of $5,000 or imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: At present, a conviction for this offence attracts a fine of $5,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months, or both.

sections.label: Adjusting maximum imprisonment term
sections.summary: The Ministry could adjust the maximum imprisonment under section 40X from three to six months, harmonising it with section 177(1) of the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Additionally, could the Ministry adjust the maximum term of imprisonment under section 40X from three to six months?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This harmonises the maximum term of imprisonment to that of section 177(1) of the Penal Code.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: Notwithstanding the above, the speaker supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, notwithstanding the above, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Bill amendment on carbon emissions
sections.summary: The amendment gives the Government legal powers to set regulatory standards on manufacture, import of goods and certain works to limit carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment to the Bill under consideration provides the Government the legal powers to set regulatory standards on the manufacture and import of certain goods as well as the carrying out of certain works in order to limit the amount of carbon emissions.

sections.label: Regulatory standards and carbon taxes
sections.summary: The optimal policy tools likely include both regulatory standards and carbon taxes, which Singapore introduced in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The set of optimal policy tools most likely includes both the setting of regulatory standards as well as the use of carbon taxes, which Singapore introduced in 2019.

sections.label: Construction site noise exemptions
sections.summary: Construction sites beyond 150 metres of homes and noise-sensitive buildings such as hospitals are exempted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Construction sites beyond 150 metres of homes and noise-sensitive buildings such as hospitals are exempted.

sections.label: Video cameras and temperature targets
sections.summary: It asks how to ensure errant contractors' video cameras work and record without deliberate intervention, and says temperature rise targets will be exceeded unless more is done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, how can we ensure that the video cameras installed by errant contractors are working well and recording without deliberate intervention?

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In fact, the target of 1.5 degrees celsius and two degrees celsius temperature rise will most certainly be exceeded unless we do more, much more.

sections.label: Sea level rise estimates
sections.summary: Current estimates say sea level will rise two to three metres at 1.5 degrees celsius and two to six metres at two degrees celsius, leaving little of Pulau Ubin above water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: With current estimates, the sea level will rise by two to three metres if the temperature rise is limited to 1.5 degrees celsius and two to six metres if limited to two degrees celsius.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: At two degrees celsius and a six-metre corresponding rise in sea level, not much of Pulau Ubin would be left above water.

sections.label: Electronic video surveillance for contractors
sections.summary: The Ministry intends to achieve this by requiring errant contractors to install electronic video surveillance systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Ministry intends to achieve this by requiring errant contractors to install electronic video surveillance systems.

sections.label: Reviewing timing of regulations
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would review when to introduce measures, given companies' difficulties from the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This will be helpful to let our residents know under what conditions the regulations are violated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, in view of the current difficulties faced by many companies due to the untamed COVID-19 pandemic, would the Ministry consider reviewing the appropriate time to introduce these measures?

sections.label: Delaying measures for SMEs
sections.summary: The passage appeals to delay some measures, citing costs of spent refrigerant collection and treatment, to give SMEs time to adjust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Mandatory collection and treatment of spent refrigerants will also entail additional costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I appeal to the Ministry to consider delaying the implementation of some of the measures during these challenging times, so as to give our SMEs more breathing room and time to adjust to the new regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   In order to ensure that construction sites remain quiet on Sundays and public holidays, the authorities will require errant contractors to install video surveillance systems.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The passage states that despite concerns and enquiries, the speaker supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding all my concerns and enquiries, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Feedback systems and surveillance support
sections.summary: The passage calls for better resident feedback systems and supports requiring errant construction sites to install electronic video surveillance systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, we should have better feedback management systems for residents to provide feedback on such matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I support the new requirement for construction sites who have contravened the no-work rule on Sundays and public holidays to install electronic video surveillance systems.

sections.label: Service standards and resident notice
sections.summary: The passage says authorities should set clear reply service standards and require advance notice to residents within 150 metres of a construction site.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The relevant authorities should ensure that clear service standards are in place as to when replies must be provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It should also be mandatory to provide advance notice to residents living within a 150-metre radius from the construction site.

sections.label: NEA video surveillance cost estimate
sections.summary: The passage asks whether NEA can give a rough estimate of installing and maintaining video surveillance equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can NEA provide a rough estimate on the cost of installation and maintenance of video surveillance equipment?

sections.label: Clarity on construction project types
sections.summary: The speaker calls for greater clarity on which types of construction projects the new amendments cover.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourth, Mr Deputy Speaker, we need greater clarity on the type of construction projects covered under the new amendments.

sections.label: Penalties for no-work rule breaches
sections.summary: The passage sets out composition and court penalties for no-work rule breaches and asks whether they are too light.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, there is a proposed penalty of a composition sum of $5,000 for construction sites that break the no-work rule for the first time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Subsequent offences lead to a Court summons with a maximum fine of $40,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If we are to meaningfully address noise pollution as a threat to public health and not just as a mere annoyance, would these penalties be too light?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As a more effective deterrent, violation of the no-work regulation ought to bear heavier consequences on the contractor’s ability to succeed at the next tender bid.

sections.label: Low-GWP refrigerant requirement start date
sections.summary: The requirement to use low-GWP refrigerants applies only to new regulated equipment supplied from 1 October 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Mr Don Wee suggested delaying the measures in view of the current economic conditions caused by the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: I wish to clarify that the requirement to use low-GWP refrigerants applies only to new regulated equipment that is supplied from 1 October 2022.

sections.label: Low-GWP chiller savings and abatement
sections.summary: CapitaLand expects $280,000 in lifecycle savings, and 10 approved or considered projects are expected to abate HFC emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: For example, CapitaLand expects to reap lifecycle cost savings of $280,000 from its low-GWP chiller deployed in Funan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: So far, 10 projects have been approved or are under consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: These projects are expected to collectively abate HFC emissions equivalent to 60 kilotonnes of carbon dioxide, comparable to taking around 18,000 cars off the road.

sections.label: Subsidies and SkillsFuture credits payment
sections.summary: Singaporeans and PRs can get up to 90% subsidies, with the $85 balance payable using SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Singaporeans and PRs will be eligible for up to 90% subsidies under SkillsFuture SG and the balance of $85 can be paid for using their SkillsFuture credits.

sections.label: HFC mitigation and Kigali Amendment review
sections.summary: HFC mitigation measures are expected to halve regulated equipment emissions by 2030, and a Kigali Amendment review is underway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The HFC mitigation measures introduced today are expected to reduce HFC emissions from the regulated equipment by around half by the year 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: With regard to the Kigali Amendment, my Ministry has initiated a review and is consulting key stakeholders.

sections.label: CCTV for breached construction sites
sections.summary: Video surveillance is required only for construction sites that breached the no-work rule, about 150 of 5,800 sites yearly, costing under 1% of project cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The requirement will only be imposed on the very small group of construction sites that have breached the no-work rule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: This is around 150 out of the 5,800 construction sites a year, or about 3% of all active sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The cost of installing video surveillance stands at less than 1% of total construction project cost on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: One set of closed-circuit television (CCTV), for example, can cost about $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Depending on the project size, a construction site that has violated the no-work rule may be required to install up to four CCTVs.

sections.label: Construction noise limits review
sections.summary: NEA will not tighten construction noise limits now due to COVID-19 impact, but will monitor and review limits with stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Given the significant impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the construction industry, this is not the time to tighten construction noise limits which will affect the whole industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I assure Mr Louis Ng that NEA will monitor the situation and continue to work with stakeholders to review construction noise limits, including the limits for construction work on Saturdays, taking into account the World Health Organization's guidelines and our local context.
